[assistant] {
  "score": 0.18,
  "gaps": [
    "Evidence grounding is very weak: roughly 1 out of the key planning claims has any cited support, and the only evidence listed is the opaque note `seed`.",
    "The artifact does not define which poker variant will be implemented, such as Texas Hold'em, five-card draw, or video poker.",
    "Game rules are not specified beyond the label `game rules`; there is no hand ranking model, betting flow, turn order, win resolution, or tie-breaking logic.",

    "The test strategy is too vague and every task has `e2e_command: (needs_backfill)`, which conflicts with the stated need for integration test coverage.",
    "Acceptance criteria are generic and not objectively verifiable.",
    "The approval gate is incomplete and all major documents remain in review-pending or draft status.",
    "No alternatives are meaningfully considered despite an `Alternatives Considered` section.",
    "No current external references are cited for poker rules, browser compatibility, accessibility expectations, or vanilla JS testing approach."
  ],
  "unsupported_claims": [
    "The project can be executed with a `parallel` strategy.",
    "`frontend_dev` alone is the right owner for both game UI and game rules.",
    "The scope covers `game ui`, `game rules`, and `test checklist` sufficiently.",
    "The success metrics are complete and can verify delivery.",
    "`Unit tests per module` and `Integration tests for cross-module flows` are an adequate test strategy.",
    "The listed risk `rule evaluation bug` is sufficiently addressed by the current plan.",
    "The generated task list is implementation-ready.",
    "The deliverables will result in a complete browser poker game.",
    "No migration is required.",
    "There are no blockers."
  ],
  "strengths": [
    "The artifact identifies the main delivery areas: UI, game rules, and testing.",
    "It correctly flags rule evaluation as a risk.",
    "It separates planning, specification, implementation design, task breakdown, and approval gate documents.",
    "It includes role hints for frontend development and QA.",
    "It explicitly records that missing e2e commands are not acceptable for completion."
  ],
  "revision_instructions": [
    "Define the exact poker variant and minimum playable loop.",
    "Replace generic Korean placeholder text with concrete English requirements, acceptance criteria, and task descriptions.",
    "Add a rules section covering deck model, shuffle/deal, hand evaluation, ranking order, tie breakers, betting or simplified action model, round lifecycle, and win conditions.",
    "Add cited references for poker hand rankings and any rule assumptions.",
    "Specify the vanilla JS file structure, UI states, controls, and state/data model.",
    "Replace all `e2e_command: (needs_backfill)` entries with real commands, for example a browser smoke test or Playwright-based integration test.",
    "Add targeted tests for hand evaluation edge cases, including straights, flushes, full houses, ace-low straights, ties, and kickers.",
    "Fill out alternatives considered, such as Texas Hold'em versus five-card draw, hand-rolled evaluator versus tested evaluator, and no-build static HTML versus a test runner setup.",
    "Update approval-gate.md only after the plan, spec, design, and tasks contain concrete, verifiable content."
  ]
